status: validation-only; not a recipe schema or planner migration
subject: Classify the finished whole recipe named by the title and supported by the ingredients. A sauce, topping, or seasoning embedded in a complete dish is not itself the recipe's physical type.

recipe_form.finished_dish: A complete food or beverage served or eaten as this recipe's result.
recipe_form.standalone_preparation: The recipe itself makes a separate sauce, seasoning, stock, dough, paste, or prepared element intended for later use or small-quantity accompaniment.
recipe_form.uncertain: The minimized content is inconsistent, merged, incomplete, or does not establish the recipe's own finished form.

queried_dish_types.soup: The recipe itself produces a finished soup or broth-based dish, including noodle soup; a stock for later cooking is base, not soup.
queried_dish_types.salad: The recipe itself produces a finished assembled salad of vegetables, grains, fruit, legumes, or protein.
queried_dish_types.vegetable: Vegetables are the defining bulk of the recipe's finished dish, not just a garnish or sauce ingredient. This may coexist with salad or soup.
queried_dish_types.condiment: The recipe itself produces a separately usable sauce, dressing, dip, relish, pickle, jam, spice blend, spread, or table seasoning. Do not select for a sauce inside a complete pasta, taco, curry, or other finished dish.
queried_dish_types.drink: The recipe itself produces a beverage intended to be drunk; a smoothie bowl eaten with a spoon is not a drink.
queried_dish_types.baking: The recipe itself produces a cake, cookie, pastry, pie, muffin, or other baked good. Exclude plain bread and dishes merely cooked in an oven.
queried_dish_types.bread: The recipe itself produces bread, flatbread, rolls, or a loaf. Do not select for a sandwich or a dish merely containing bread.
queried_dish_types.base: The recipe itself produces a foundational stock, dough, paste, or basic ingredient for later cooking, not a ready-to-eat finished meal. Do not select solely because a complete dish contains a base.
queried_dish_types.component: The recipe itself produces a standalone prepared element intended to be incorporated into another dish. Exclude complete dishes, table condiments, and foundational bases; do not select merely because a finished dish could accompany another.
queried_dish_types.snack: The recipe's physical form is discrete bite-sized or finger-food pieces such as crackers, small bites, fritters, or energy balls. This does not by itself determine whether its meal role is snack or starter.
queried_dish_types.dessert: The recipe itself produces a sweet prepared dish or treat such as pudding, ice cream, confection, cake, or sweet pastry. It may also be baking or snack.

derived_dish_type.other: Only if recipe_form is finished_dish, the physical form is clear, and none of the named physical types is supported. Never ask other as an independent probability question; do not infer it from uncertain named-type answers.

meal_roles.main: Central substantial dish of a meal, potentially served with ordinary rice or bread. Soup or salad may be main if substantial.
meal_roles.side: An accompaniment eaten in ordinary side portions with a main, not a small sauce or seasoning.
meal_roles.starter: An appetizer or first course supported by serving evidence or clearly conventional form.
meal_roles.dessert: Sweet course or treat, not primarily a breakfast or beverage.
meal_roles.breakfast: Primarily breakfast as supported by explicit title or conventional form.
meal_roles.component: Preparation for incorporation into another recipe, such as dough, stock, or cooking spice mix; not a table condiment.
meal_roles.snack: Small between-meal food, supported by explicit snack intent or conventional form. Physical finger-food form alone does not decide this role.
meal_roles.condiment: Small-quantity table accompaniment, spread, dip, pickle, or seasoning rather than a meal or ordinary side.
meal_roles.uncertain: The available evidence is missing, inconsistent, or supports several roles without a defensible primary role.

input: Reviewed name, servings, and ingredient item/amount/unit only. No stored categories, chapters, source URL, methods, notes, household fields, preferences, history, or adaptations leave the local runtime. Open local method/serving evidence only for review, never as an unreviewed outbound fallback.
sampling: A separately frozen simple random sample of 300 IDs from the 3,493-ID deployable snapshot for a reviewer-agreement estimate, plus a disjoint targeted supplement for rare roles and known failure modes. Keep denominators separate. Split representative sample into tuning and locked holdout before inference; report exclusions and abstentions in the original selected-ID denominator.
calibration: Preserve raw per-label probabilities. Tune thresholds only on the designated tuning subset against independent review; freeze them before assessing the holdout. Report per-type precision, recall, abstention and coverage, as well as meal-role confusion. Do not treat model confidence or stored labels as ground truth.
application_boundary: Read-only classification and review queue. Do not rewrite category.dish_type or category.meal_role from model output. The live planner still consumes legacy role-like dish_type tags, so physical-type migration needs a separate compatibility design and independent production verification.
